structured_output.summary: Transit on target, Rp 4.53 Re, FPP 0.01, no secondary; RUWE 3.01 needs follow-up.
reasons: The signal is new: exofop_tois, exofop_ctois and published_signal are all empty, and the step-1 cross-match found no TOI, CTOI, TCE or TESS EB match in the catalogues of 2026-10-29.

The transit is real and repeats across five sectors: joint_search_snr 18.3 against joint_search_highest_null_snr 5.5, and each sector recovers it near expectation (S10 SNR 7.5 vs 9.8 expected, S64 7.7 vs 8.5, S99 11.4 vs 11.1, S100 11.2 vs 12.1). The all-sector figure shows a clear dip in every sector.

The companion is planet-sized: planet_radius_earth_radii 4.53 +/- 0.34 (fit_radius_ratio 0.0214, stellar_radius_solar_radii 1.94), transit_grazing False, fit_impact_parameter 0.392, so the radius is constrained and far below the 22.4 Earth-radius stellar limit; stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio 1.22 is consistent with the transit being on a star like the target.

No eclipsing-binary signatures: secondary_depth_ppm 16 +/- 23 (against secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm 152), ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm -70 +/- 52 with no companion mass detected, odd_even_difference_sigma 0.85, and sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.422 for the fitted depths (S101 570, S10 455, S64 541, S99 584, S100 555 ppm).

The dip is localised on the target when all sectors are combined: joint_difference_image_snr 6.3, joint_best_source TIC 273213461, joint_pixel_verdict on target; the S101 and S100 difference images show the brightest pixel at the target. TRICERATOPS gives fpp_mean 0.01005 and nfpp_mean 1.066e-08 with nearby_scenarios_excluded True, most_likely_scenario TP on TIC 273213461.

Caution weighed, not decisive: gaia_ruwe 3.01 (gaia_non_single_star 0) suggests an unresolved companion, and gaia_rv_variable True (gaia_rv_epoch_scatter_km_s 10.3, gaia_rv_epoch_range_km_s 48.8 over 38 transits). However gaia_vbroad_km_s 60.7 means the per-epoch RVs are poorly measured, and the derived gaia_rv_semi_amplitude_upper_limit_km_s 14.6 limits any companion at this period to gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses 0.082, i.e. below a stellar mass. A bound companion would dilute the depth and make the true radius larger, so the submission should flag that high-resolution imaging and RVs are needed.

Caution weighed, not decisive: gaia_neighbours 64 with 41 listed as able to cause the dip (nearest Gaia DR3 5369078040516638592 at 10" G 19.1 needing 47%), and cutout_sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.00617 shows aperture-dependent depths differ between sectors (S10 r1.5-r3.0 719-872 ppm vs S101 455-502 ppm). The per-sector pixel checks are individually too faint (SNR 1.8-4.5), so the on-target verdict rests on the joint SNR 6.3. This is adequate for a CTOI but is the weakest link; the four unreleased sectors (unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star 111 112 113 114) will roughly double the pixel data and should be re-run when released.

I agree with the mechanical decision. The remaining doubts (RUWE 3.01, crowding) are ones that more TESS sectors cannot settle on their own and that ground-based follow-up prompted by a CTOI can; a 4.5 Earth-radius body at P 0.857 d around a 1.94 solar-radius star sits in the hot-Neptune desert and is worth that follow-up.
